Article Title: 'Paying price for being a woman, Muslim': Congress slams SC bail order in Bilkis Bano case
Article Text:
Congress slams SC bail order in Bilkis Bano case

NEW DELHI: The Congress on Tuesday criticised the Supreme Court 's decision to suspend the life sentences of two convicts in the Bilkis Bano gangrape and murder case, saying she was being subjected to fresh "humiliation" and trauma.The party said the treatment meted out to her reflected the price women, particularly Muslim women, had to pay for seeking justice.Congress media and publicity department head Pawan Khera said Bilkis Bano had issued a statement expressing shock over the order, stating that she was neither informed of the proceedings nor given an opportunity to be heard. He added that she had announced her intention to challenge the decision."As if the cruel and gruesome crime committed against her was not enough, she is now being made to endure fresh humiliation and trauma. That is the price one has to pay for being a woman, and even more so for being a Muslim," Khera said in a post on X.In a statement issued through senior advocate Shobha Gupta, Bano said she learnt about the Supreme Court's October 28 order through media reports and questioned how the decision could have been taken without hearing her.She said this was the second time an order concerning the case had been passed without giving her an opportunity to present her views."I still cannot believe that once again, for the second time, an order has been passed by the Supreme Court without calling me up and without hearing me. I learnt of this through press reports," she said.A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and PB Varale suspended the life sentences of Bipin Chandra Joshi and Pradeep Mordhiya, granting them bail on October 28. The court noted that both convicts had spent more than 17 years in prison and that one of them had a severe handicap."Having heard the parties, suffice it to state that the appellants have been under incarceration for a period of more than 17 years, and also the fact remains that one of the appellants has a severe handicap. Certainly, there are issues to be decided in the appeal, both on fact and law," the court said in its order."In view of the above and considering the issues involved in this appeal, we suspend the sentence and grant bail to the appellants on such terms and conditions as may be imposed by the concerned trial court," it added.Bano was 21 years old and five months pregnant when she was gang-raped while fleeing the communal riots that broke out in Gujarat in February 2002 following the Godhra train burning incident. Her three-year-old daughter was among the seven family members killed.Joshi and Mordhiya were among the 11 men whose remission was quashed by the Supreme Court in 2024. Bano has said she will challenge the latest order granting bail to the two convicts.
Article Summary: Congress criticises Supreme Court's decision to suspend life sentences of two convicts in the Bilkis Bano gangrape and murder case. The party said the treatment meted out to Bano reflected the price women, particularly Muslim women, had to pay for seeking justice. Bano was 21 years old and five months pregnant when she was gang-raped while fleeing the communal riots in 2002.

Article Title: At Sonia's book launch, Gandhis open up about love, loss, and bad chicken
Article Text:
Sonia Gandhi's book launch on Monday.

NEW DELHI: "And listen, if you want to fall in love, go to Varsity Restaurant in Cambridge. But never eat the chicken chasseur, okay?" Rahul Gandhi jokingly delivered this piece of advice at the launch of his mother Sonia Gandhi 's memoir, 'Belonging: A Journey of Love', in Delhi on Monday. Years after hearing the story about his parents' first meeting in Cambridge, he recounted how he went to the Varsity Restaurant with his girlfriend to see where they had met.When Rahul told the man at the entrance that his parents had met there, the man said he knew exactly who they were and recommended the chicken chasseur from the menu. However, the meal did not live up to its romantic legacy. Rahul contrasts his parents' memories of the restaurant with his own experience. "They seem to remember that the food was fantastic. The food's horrible!" he said as the audience laughed.The anecdote was part of a series of family recollections the leader of the opposition shared after saying he had been instructed to avoid politics. However, many read a political subtext into the seating arrangements. In the front row was an array of opposition leaders such as Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav; Trinamool Congress MP Abhishek Banerjee; National Conference president Farooq Abdullah; Supriya Sule of NCP-SP; Jharkhand CM Hemant Soren; and Tamil Nadu CM C Joseph Vijay.Also in the front row was former Punjab CM Captain Amarinder Singh, who left Congress in 2021 following a bitter falling-out with the Gandhis.Rahul name-checked Amarinder and mentioned that he had seen his parents fight only once. Rajiv Gandhi was speaking to Amarinder on phone when Sonia tried several times to tell him something. Rajiv was stressed and eventually got angry. "We saw them argue many times, but that was the only time we ever saw them fight," Rahul said.Sonia Gandhi too kept the conversation away from politics. Asked why she chose to write a memoir when she had guarded her privacy fiercely in the past, she said she wanted to set the record straight about her family amid "unreal stories" woven around them. "So much has been said about my mother-in-law, husband, son, daughter, and myself; and most of it is unreal. It has really nothing to do with the way we are. Stories are woven around you, untruths are woven around you, and hurtful things are said which are nowhere near the truth. And I thought, well, perhaps this was a way of bringing out my feelings, what I know of my family, and maybe people will be open to listening to my story too," the Rajya Sabha MP said.She recalled feeling like an outsider when she first moved to India, conscious of making mistakes. She connected that experience to Indian women who enter a new family after marriage and have to adjust to its ways. The memoir's title, she said, reflected "the effort to be accepted and to belong, to finally belong."While she recounted a story of how she and Rajiv would go to India Gate to have ice cream (she had a favourite Sardarji ice cream vendor), Rahul spoke of his parents' affection and a habit he had assumed was common in every home: "Every meal there would be Papa and on Papa's lap there would be Mama." He said he realised it was unusual only when he visited friends' homes.But things changed after the assassinations of Indira Gandhi and Rajiv Gandhi, he said, "The fun-loving mother, the smiling mother disappeared." Sonia, once an extrovert, withdrew into herself.Rahul also spoke of his mother's resilience in the face of cancer, saying he had never seen her afraid or back down. He ended by telling her how proud he believed Rajiv would have been of her: "Mummy, Papa loved you. But I cannot even tell you how proud he would be of you."
Article Summary: Sonia Gandhi's memoir, 'Belonging: A Journey of Love', launched in Delhi on Monday. She said she wanted to set the record straight about her family amid "unreal stories" woven around them. The memoir's title reflected "the effort to be accepted and to belong, to finally belong"

Article Title: 'I am scared once again': Bilkis Bano releases statement after SC grants bail to two convicts
Article Text:
Bilkis said she was scared for herself, her family and her children, adding that the decision had shaken her faith in the justice system

NEW DELHI: Bilkis Bano said that "familiar fears are resurfacing" after the Supreme Court suspended the sentences and granted bail to two of the 11 men convicted of gang-raping her and murdering 14 members of her family during the 2002 Gujarat riots.In a statement issued on Monday, she expressed shock and disbelief over the order, saying she was neither informed about the proceedings nor given an opportunity to be heard."I still cannot believe that once again, for the second time, an order has been passed by the Supreme Court without calling me up and without hearing me. I learnt of this through press reports," she said.The Supreme Court bench of Justices M M Sudresh and P B Varale passed the order on October 28, which was uploaded on Monday. Reacting to the development, Bilkis said she was scared for herself, her family and her children, adding that the decision had shaken her faith in the justice system."For 24 years I have searched for and found reservoirs of courage I did not know I had, only because a million voices of support and solidarity came my way," she said, recalling her long fight for justice following the assault and the murder of her family members.Bilkis, who was 19 at the time of the 2002 incident, said she had spent years rebuilding her life with the support of family and friends and had hoped to find peace. However, the latest order had brought back the fears she thought she had overcome."Yet today I find myself losing the very justice I had fought so hard to win. Familiar fears are resurfacing. I am scared once again. For myself, my family, and my children. And I am scared of losing faith in justice, yet again," she said.Questioning why the court had not ensured that her voice was heard before passing the order, Bilkis said she would challenge the decision."I will fight this order. I must," she said, adding that she was doing so for her children and the memory of her three-year-old daughter Saleha, as well as for women everywhere."Because no woman, no survivor, no citizen should have to endure this eternal test of belonging and equality, and fight for justice for the rest of her life," she said.Bilkis Bano was 21 years old and five months pregnant when she was gang-raped while trying to escape the horror of the communal riots that broke out after the Godhra train burning incident in February 2002. Her three-year-old daughter was among the seven family members killed.
Article Summary: Bilkis Bano says she is scared for herself, her family and her children. She says she was neither informed about the proceedings nor given an opportunity to be heard. The Supreme Court bench of Justices M M Sudresh and P B Varale passed the order on October 28, which was uploaded on Monday.

Article Title: Indian inventor patents new technique to transmute elements, reports gold in tests
Article Text:
Bengaluru inventor Rajah Vijay Kumar has patented a frequency-based process called GNT that he claims transmutes elements, with lab tests reporting gold and silver in processed samples

How it works

.

Larger ambition

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BENGALURU: What if one chemical element could be converted into several others, including gold? An Indian inventor from Bengaluru has received a patent for a process that could do this using specially generated frequencies, without conventional nuclear reactors or radioactive reactions.There is no fission or fusion reaction here. His experiments report the presence of gold, silver and several other elements in processed samples.Rajah Vijay Kumar’s invention, called Gravitoradiophysical Nuclear Transmutation (GNT), has been granted Indian patent (No. 5683222), nearly eight years after it was filed on Nov 21, 2017. The patent was granted in the second half of 2025.“The GNT could eventually find applications in energy, medicine, genetics, industry and space,” Kumar, director and chief scientific officer, Scalene Energy Research Institute, Organization de Scalene Foundation, told TOI.To understand the process, it helps to know what makes one element different from another. Every element has atoms, and at the centre of each atom is a nucleus. The number of protons in this nucleus determines the element’s identity.Gold, for example, has 79 protons, while mercury has 80. Turning mercury into gold would therefore require changing the structure of its nucleus by removing (or displacing) one proton and one electron, something an ordinary chemical reaction cannot do.Kumar’s proposed process uses a specially designed reactor to achieve this. Its central component, called the ‘Boom Tube’, a tubular reactor that produces continuous free fall and weightlessness at molecular levels, fitted with antennas made from an aluminium alloy and connected to a high power high frequency generator. The apparatus also has systems to regulate temperature and pressure in a vacuum environment.The process works in two proposed stages. First, one frequency is used to separate the target element from the chemical compound containing it. A second frequency is then applied to bring about the proposed change in the element's nucleus.The process works in two proposed stages. First, a disassociating frequency depending on the interested elements is used to separate the target element from the chemical compound containing it. Then, an element specific transmutation frequency is then applied to bring about the proposed change in the element's nucleus. The exact mechanism of action is still being studied.As Kumar explains: “Every element has a unique frequency, or set of frequencies, that can break its chemical bonds and separate it from a compound. For the initial experiments, I chose mercury, which it describes as one of the heavier elements that could be handled relatively safely in its experimental setup. The aim, however, was not simply to make gold.”The larger ambition was to develop a process that can convert different elements and isotopes for possible applications in energy, medicine, industry and space exploration.The patent describes experiments in which a mercury compound, mercuric sulphate, was mixed with distilled water and processed through the reactor. An untreated portion was retained for comparison. An accredited laboratory, reportedly unaware of which samples had been processed, analysed both.The results reported gold at 1.91 mg per litre in the first processed sample and 2.3 milligrams per litre in the second. Silver was also detected at 11 milligrams per litre in the second test. Other elements, including magnesium, manganese, phosphorus and zinc, were reported in the processed samples. The mercury came down from 33.45 gm to 8.67 gm while sulphur almost remained unchanged at around 8.5 gm.The laboratory used a technique called Inductively Coupled Plasma Atomic Emission Spectroscopy (ICP-AES), which identifies and measures the quantities of elements in a sample. The research team acknowledges that considerable work under different conditions remains before the process can be perfected or considered for large-scale applications.There is also an important scientific caveat. Detecting gold, silver or other elements in a sample does not, by itself, mean the technology or process is ready for wider use immediately. The laboratory technique measures what is present, not how it was formed. Independent experiments, including tests of the elements’ atomic structure, would be needed to understand exactly the science of how such claimed transmutation has occurred.
Article Summary: Inventor Rajah Vijay Kumar has patented a frequency-based process called GNT that he claims transmutes elements. His experiments report the presence of gold, silver and several other elements in processed samples. Independent experiments, including tests of the elements’ atomic structure, would be needed to understand exactly how such claimed transmutation has occurred.

Article Title: Congress forms screening committees for 5 poll-bound states; Ajay Maken to head UP panel

Who heads the screening panels

NEW DELHI: The Congress on Monday constituted screening committees for five states scheduled to hold assembly elections, with party president Mallikarjun Kharge appointing senior leaders to head the panels. Ajay Maken will lead the committee for Uttar Pradesh , while Sirivella Prasad has been named chairperson of the Punjab panel.The committees have also been formed for Uttarakhand, Goa and Manipur. Each panel comprises a chairperson and two other members and will be responsible for the party's screening process ahead of the elections.For Uttar Pradesh, Maken will be joined by Aslam Shaikh and B V Srinivas. The Punjab committee will be headed by Sirivella Prasad, with Sachin Sawant and Nivedith Alva as members.In Uttarakhand, Deepa Dasmunsi will chair the panel, which includes Anil Chaudhary and Pal Bhai Ambaliya. KJ George will head the Goa committee, with Satej D Patil and Shafi Parambil as members.For Manipur, B M Sandeep has been appointed chairperson. Hibi Eden and Rajesh Thakur are the other members of the committee.
Article Summary: Kharge appoints screening panels for five poll-bound states. Ajay Maken will lead the committee for Uttar Pradesh. Sirivella Prasad has been named chairperson of the Punjab panel. committees have also been formed for Uttarakhand, Goa and Manipur.

Article Title: Census Phase-II starts in 4 poll-bound states, postponed in Manipur
Article Text:
The exercise has been postponed in Manipur until further notice amid demands for an NRC first.

New Delhi: Self-enumeration for the population enumeration phase of Census 2027 began on Monday in UP, Punjab, Goa and non-snow-bound areas of Uttarakhand. It will run till Nov 30, followed by house-to-house enumeration from Dec 1. The exercise will collect data across 40 fields, including caste. The question is open-ended and reply will be recorded as declared by the respondent. No documentary proof or verification is required.MHA's Sept 5 notification advanced the exercise in the four states ahead of assembly polls early next year. It will run till Jan 4, 2027, followed by a revisional round from Jan 5 to 9.Though Manipur is due for assembly polls, the census there has been postponed until further notice amid demands for a National Register of Citizens (NRC) exercise first. Houselisting operations, Phase I, are complete in all 35 states/UTs except Manipur.In remaining states/UTs, population enumeration will be held from Jan 25 to Feb 28, 2027, followed by a revisional round from Mar 1 to 5. Self-enumeration will be available from Jan 10 to 24. For the first time, Census 2027 is using digital tools. The web-based self-enumeration facility is available in 16 Indian languages. Information collected under the Census Act, 1948, will remain confidential.
Article Summary: Self-enumeration for the population enumeration phase of Census 2027 began on Monday in UP, Punjab, Goa and non-snow-bound areas of Uttarakhand. NEW DELHI: When the first gallery of Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum with ‘Adornment’ as its theme opens at the iconic North Block later next year, the 4,500-year-old bronze figurine known as the ‘Dancing Girl of Mohenjo-Daro’, currently at National Museum, will be moved to the new facility as a key display to showcase India’s civilisational journey.Sharing details, culture secretary Vivek Aggarwal said among the prime objects, which are likely to be on the display at YYBM’s inaugural gallery, visitors can also expect to see the Nizam’s jewels that are currently at RBI under a high-security custodial arrangement.Several objects are likely to be moved from the National Museum to the ‘Adornment’ gallery. Visitors will be able to see ancient gold and gem-studded jewellery from Taxila (Taksasila) currently placed at the National Museum. Miniature paintings, sculptures from the collection from Indian Museum in Kolkata and Gandhara collection of sculptures will also be showcased.According to the ministry, the content team is curating the display plan for objects to be taken from museums to YYBM. “This proposed arrangement by the content team will be presented before an advisory committee that will look at the entire description and selection of objects and approve the final plan.We want to showcase the sophistication of Indian culture from the beginning...,” the secretary said.“National Museum will remain a museum of history. YYBM is focused on the civilisational journey so there is a distinct differentiation between both of them. The objects at YYBM will come from different museums of the country, including the National Museum,” he added.Last week, the cabinet committee on economic affairs cleared a Rs 3,230 crore development plan that will include North and South Block and will be spread over nearly 1.8 lakh square metres .The project scheduled to be complete by March 2031 is being pitched as the museum with the largest display area in the world.

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Tuesday pulled up Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut over his remarks targeting Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and the judiciary. The court observed that apologies should come from the heart and not the mind.A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi was hearing the contempt case filed by the Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA). Raut appeared physically before the court, while Waghle joined the proceedings virtually, in compliance with the court's earlier directions.During the hearing, SCBA president and senior advocate Pradeep Rai told the bench that although Raut had apologised for his comments, he had subsequently made social media posts against the Supreme Court. Rai also pointed out that Raut had shared a photograph of the Supreme Court of Albania being set on fire by protesters.Justice Kumar reminded Raut of the responsibility that came with his experience as a politician and parliamentarian."Mr. Sanjay Raut, you are a seasoned politician, we have been hearing your speeches from advocate days. You are a seasoned parliamentarian, and you yourself were in the press. You should know what should be the restraint," he said, as reported by LiveLaw.The Supreme Court had issued show-cause notices to Raut and Waghle on October 16 over their alleged remarks against the CJI and the judiciary.The contempt proceedings stem from the controversy surrounding CJI Surya Kant's decision to decline a request for a personal meeting by a delegation of opposition leaders, asking them instead to approach the court through a petition.According to the SCBA's petition, Waghle had posted an alleged abusive remark against the CJI on X in response to a report about the decision, before deleting it and issuing an apology.Raut, meanwhile, had allegedly questioned the conduct of judges, claiming that some had attended political programmes organised by the BJP and participated in dinners hosted by chief ministers.

NEW DELHI: Prince William and Kate Middleton on Tuesday visited Bandra Reclamation Garden in Mumbai, where the Prince drove an electric three-wheeler with the Princess of Wales as a passenger. The royal couple also interacted with the 15 finalists of The Earthshot Prize 2026 from across the world.The event, set against the backdrop of the Bandra-Worli Sea Link, gathered finalists who are developing innovative answers to environmental problems.India’s representatives among the 15 finalists are Mahindra Last Mile Mobility and Mahila Housing Trust, ANI reported.The meeting was a key engagement before the Earthshot Prize awards ceremony, which India is hosting for the first time. Five winners will be announced later on Tuesday, and each will receive Euro 1 million to help expand their environmental solutions.The Earthshot Prize honours innovative approaches to environmental challenges, and this year it has taken its global platform to India, spotlighting solutions aimed at protecting and restoring the planet.On Monday, the first day of their Mumbai trip, Prince William and Kate had a packed schedule that included riding the Mumbai Metro, playing gully cricket with school students and meeting cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar.The couple landed in Mumbai on Monday for the annual environmental awards, which Prince William founded in 2020. They attended the Earthshot Prize 2026 Impact Assembly, where the Prince talked about India’s role in finding solutions to environmental challenges.In his speech, Prince William commended India’s work on clean energy and sustainable development. He also said economic growth and environmental protection could go hand in hand.“There is a phrase in Hindi: ‘Rang Birangi Duniya’. A world full of colour. Perhaps that is how we should see the future. Not in black and white, and not presented as a series of false choices between people and the planet, prosperity and nature, but in all its colours. A world in which solutions can come from anywhere,” he said.After their Mumbai engagements, Prince William and Kate will travel to New Delhi, where they will meet Prime Minister Narendra Modi This is the couple’s second official visit to India. They previously visited together in 2016, when they also travelled to Bhutan.The 2026 Earthshot Prize awards cover five categories: Protect and restore nature, Clean our air, Revive our oceans, Build a waste-free world and Fix our climate.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Tuesday agreed to hear on Wednesday a plea filed by the Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) seeking contempt action against a lawyer who allegedly made unsavoury remarks against Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant during court proceedings.The plea was mentioned for urgent listing before a bench comprising the CJI and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana. SCBA secretary Pragya Baghel and joint secretary Meenesh Dubey mentioned the matter before the bench.They informed the court that the association had obtained the consent of Attorney General R Venkataramani to file a petition seeking the initiation of criminal contempt proceedings against the lawyer.The development follows an incident on Monday, when the lawyer was escorted out of a Supreme Court courtroom after allegedly making unsubstantiated and unsavoury remarks against the CJI.The incident began when the lawyer made an unscheduled mention of a petition filed on November 2, claiming it had not been listed despite the CJI's office being informed.The bench was hearing motor accident compensation cases at the time.The court objected to the unscheduled mention and asked the lawyer to approach the registrar to have his request for early listing included.The lawyer said he had already apologised and wanted to know why the petition had not been listed. When the CJI said he would look into the matter, the lawyer allegedly reacted by questioning his position and integrity.“No, I will not wait. You cannot sit in that chair. You do not deserve. You do not have the integrity for that,” the lawyer told the CJI.A registry official said that petitions were listed through court software and that the CJI had little role in the process.The official also said several petitions had been filed before November 6, after which the court remained closed for a week for Diwali.The lawyer's conduct drew objections from members of the Bar, some of whom met the CJI and requested that contempt proceedings be initiated against him.The SCBA has now moved to seek criminal contempt action, with its office-bearers informing the Supreme Court that they had secured the Attorney General's consent to file the plea.The matter is scheduled to be heard on Wednesday.

Article Title: IISc researchers find antibiotic combination to reverse drug resistance in TB
Article Text:
Colonies of M. tuberculosis growing in an agar plate | Pic Credit: IISc

Authors of the study: (left to right) Nagasuma Chandra (corresponding author), Amit Singh (co-author), Sukriti Pal (co-author), Shalini Birua (co-author) | Pic Credit: IISc

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BENGALURU: Researchers from the Indian Institute of Science (IISc) have identified an antibiotic combination that can reverse resistance to isoniazid, a frontline drug for tuberculosis (TB), in laboratory tests and in mice. TB remains one of the world's most persistent health challenges.The study, titled “Vancomycin rescues sensitivity to isoniazid in clinical isolates of drug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis,” has been published in Microbiology Spectrum.The team from IISc’s department of biochemistry paired isoniazid with vancomycin. The combination sharply reduced bacterial growth in clinical isolates from drug-resistant TB patients and lowered bacterial load in mice infected with multidrug-resistant (MDR) ‘M tuberculosis’, according to IISc.Isoniazid is a prodrug, which means a bacterial enzyme must activate it before it can work. Mutations in certain genes can block this activation, letting the bacteria survive. Growing resistance has become a major challenge in TB treatment.Vancomycin, used against several bacterial infections, normally struggles to cross the highly impermeable cell wall of M. tuberculosis. The researchers report that when the two drugs are given together, the cell wall loses integrity, allowing vancomycin to enter and kill the bacteria.The team tested isolates from sputum samples of patients with drug-resistant TB, working with the National Tuberculosis Institute, Bengaluru. They showed a broad range of isoniazid resistance, allowing the team to test the combination against different resistance mechanisms.The combination substantially outperformed either drug alone. Most isolates showed more than 90% reduction in bacterial growth, including isoniazid-resistant and MDR strains.The team then tested the combination in mice infected with MDR M. tuberculosis, in collaboration with Amit Singh, professor at IISc's Centre for Infectious Disease Research and department of microbiology and cell biology.After 10 days of treatment, neither drug alone significantly reduced bacterial burden. Together, they cut bacterial load about 10-fold in both lungs and spleen. Lung tissue also showed fewer granulomas, inflammatory structures that form as the body tries to contain TB infection.“Isoniazid resistance poses a major challenge in the treatment of TB. To tackle this problem, we started exploring ways to rescue the drug by reversing resistance,” said Nagasuma Chandra, professor at the department of biochemistry and corresponding author of the study.“Although several antibiotic combinations are available for TB treatment, we continue to face challenges due to drug-resistance. Our study identifies a drug treatment strategy that can reverse resistance to isoniazid, an otherwise highly effective antibiotic,” said Sukriti Pal, a PhD student and the study's first author.The study's authors include Pal, Shalini Birua, Singh and Chandra, among others. The combination is not yet ready for use in patients. The team is working to advance it towards clinical trials.“Before the combination can be considered for use in patients, its safety and efficacy need to be studied much more extensively. Clinical trials need to be conducted on drug-resistant TB cases,” Pal said.
Article Summary: Researchers from the Indian Institute of Science (IISc) have identified an antibiotic combination that can reverse resistance to isoniazid, a frontline drug for tuberculosis. The team from IISc’s department of biochemistry paired isoniaZid with vancomycin. The combination sharply reduced bacterial growth in clinical isolates from drug-resistant TB patients and lowered bacterial load in mice.

Article Title: Presidential election today? Trump confuses India with Brazil, claims 125 million voted
Article Text:
Trump says "125 million Indians voted in presidential election today."

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the same day!”He then compared the alleged election results with the US electoral process, writing, “In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian "presidential election" He also questioned the integrity of the American voting system. India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college.

The wait is almost over for IPL fans, with all 10 franchises set to submit their list of retained and released players for the 2027 season on Tuesday, November 17.The original deadline was November 15, but the BCCI extended it by two days. The change reportedly came because the earlier date coincided with the fifth and final ODI between India and New Zealand.With several big player trades already completed, the retention announcements are expected to bring more clarity on the squads ahead of the IPL 2027 mini-auction.All 10 franchises must submit their list of retained and released players to the BCCI by Tuesday, November 17, 2026.The teams will reveal which players they want to keep for the next season and which ones they have decided to release. The remaining amount will be available to the franchise at the mini-auction.The IPL 2027 mini-auction will be held in Goa on December 16, 2026.Since this is a mini-auction, teams will have the opportunity to strengthen their squads by signing players released by other franchises and those who enter the auction pool.Several high-profile trades have already taken place ahead of the retention deadline. Mumbai Indians and Punjab Kings were involved in a major exchange involving Hardik Pandya and Arshdeep Singh.Rishabh Pant has also returned to Delhi Capitals, while Kuldeep Yadav has moved to Lucknow Super Giants.Sunrisers Hyderabad have been among the busiest teams in the trade market. T Natarajan has returned to the franchise, with Zeeshan Ansari moving to Delhi Capitals.SRH have also brought in Khaleel Ahmed and Nathan Ellis from Chennai Super Kings in exchange for Liam Livingstone and Jack Edwards.

India pacer Gurnoor Brar has been reprimanded by the International Cricket Council (ICC) for breaching its Code of Conduct during the fourth ODI against New Zealand in Mount Maunganui. The 25-year-old was penalised for his aggressive celebration following the dismissal of New Zealand batter Tim Seifert Brar was found guilty of violating Article 2.5 of the ICC Code of Conduct for Players and Player Support Personnel, which relates to the use of language, actions or gestures that disparage a batter or could provoke an aggressive reaction following their dismissal in an international match.The incident occurred at the end of the 12th over after Seifert was dismissed. Brar celebrated in a manner that was considered aggressive and potentially demeaning towards the batter, with the possibility of provoking an equally aggressive response.Apart from an official reprimand, one demerit point was added to Brar's disciplinary record. It was his second offence within a 24-month period, taking his accumulated tally to two demerit points.Brar admitted the offence and accepted the sanction proposed by Ranjan Madugalle of the Emirates ICC International Panel of Match Referees, meaning there was no requirement for a formal hearing.On-field umpires Chris Brown and Kumar Dharmasena, third umpire Paul Reiffel and fourth umpire Wayne Knights levelled the charge.Level 1 breaches of the ICC Code of Conduct carry a minimum penalty of an official reprimand and a maximum sanction of 50 per cent of a player's match fee, along with one or two demerit points.Brar's disciplinary action comes at a time when he has also earned a place in India's Test squad for the upcoming two-match series against New Zealand, beginning November 19.India have released spinner Kuldeep Yadav from the Test squad, with the visitors expecting seam-friendly conditions during the series.India clinched the ODI series 3-1 after having earlier beaten New Zealand 3-2 in the preceding T20I series.
Article Summary: Gurnoor Brar has been reprimanded by the International Cricket Council for breaching its Code of Conduct. The 25-year-old was penalised for his aggressive celebration following the dismissal of New Zealand batter Tim Seifert. Brar admitted the offence and accepted the sanction.

His journey shows how much a parent’s support can matter in a child’s life.Ed Kelce grew up in Cleveland, Ohio, where he developed an interest in football and baseball. Having played both sports himself, he understood how much they could teach children. When Jason and Travis were young, he wanted them to enjoy sports without feeling forced to follow a particular path.He started getting involved when the boys were very little. Ed coached Travis in T-ball and Jason in coach-pitch baseball. He also spent time playing with them in the front yard and created space in the family garage where they could practise.One of his favourite memories goes back to when Jason was still a toddler. His son would roll a ball towards him on the living-room floor, and Ed would roll it back. It was a simple activity, but it became one of their earliest shared memories.Years later, while appearing on the brothers’ New Heights podcast, Ed explained how he viewed his responsibility as a father.“My job is to help you find a passion, and then feed that passion. Whatever you want to do, I’m there.”He wanted both boys to discover what they enjoyed and then work towards becoming better at it. He also believed that talent needed to be supported by hard work. Rather than always placing them in situations where they could easily succeed, he encouraged them to compete and learn from more difficult experiences.That approach helped Jason and Travis develop their interest in football. Both eventually attended the University of Cincinnati, where they played college football before entering the NFL.Raising two children with serious sporting ambitions required time, money and a lot of planning. Jason and Travis played different sports and had busy schedules, so their parents had to manage practices, competitions, travel and equipment costs.Ed worked in the steel industry before moving into sales, while Donna built her career in banking. Both had professional responsibilities, but they made sure their sons received the support they needed.The financial side was not always easy. The family had to plan its spending around the boys’ sporting activities, including equipment, travel and other expenses. Ed and Donna had to make choices to ensure both children could take part in the activities they enjoyed.They also divided their parenting responsibilities carefully. Donna explained on New Heights that they worked as a team. When one parent travelled with Jason for a game, the other stayed home with Travis. This allowed both boys to receive attention and support, even when their schedules clashed.Donna described their arrangement as being “like a tag team with you two.”It was not always possible for both parents to attend every event, but they made sure someone was there. Their priority was to give Jason and Travis equal opportunities rather than allowing one child’s sporting commitments to take over family life.Neither Ed nor Donna knew that their sons would eventually become NFL stars. They were simply making sure the boys had the chance to explore their interests and work towards their goals.While Ed and Donna were busy raising their sons, their own marriage was going through a difficult period. The couple had been married for nearly 25 years, but their relationship was not always happy.Travis spoke about this in the Prime Video documentary Kelce. He remembered noticing during childhood that his parents did not share a bedroom. As he reached middle school, he began to understand that their marriage was struggling.Despite their personal problems, Ed and Donna continued raising their sons together. They knew that separating while Jason and Travis were still studying and playing sports would make an already busy family life more difficult.Ed explained their decision in the documentary, saying, “If we had split as we probably both would have preferred, that would have been a nightmare with the logistics, getting kids where they had to be and providing all the support.”His words give an idea of the practical challenges they were trying to avoid. They had to manage school, sports, travel and other family responsibilities, and both understood how much their sons depended on them.Their marriage eventually ended in divorce after Jason and Travis had graduated from college. However, their separation did not end their responsibilities as parents. They continued to support their sons and remained connected as a family.Donna has also spoken warmly about Ed and their years together, making it clear that she does not regret the family they built.Ed’s involvement did not end when his sons left home for college. When Jason joined the Philadelphia Eagles and Travis became a star with the Kansas City Chiefs, he continued attending games and following their careers.Supporting both sons became more challenging once they started playing for different NFL teams. Their games were often held in different cities, making it difficult for Ed and Donna to be present at every match. They continued dividing their time so both brothers could receive support.One of the most memorable moments came during Super Bowl LVII in February 2023, when Jason’s Eagles faced Travis’s Chiefs. It was an unusual situation for the family because one son would celebrate winning the championship while the other would have to deal with defeat.Ed understood how difficult that could be. Before the game, he explained that he wanted to be with whichever son lost.“Somebody’s gonna feel pretty crummy and I wanna be with him-initially.”He also joked that he had already won because both his sons had reached the Super Bowl.The game ended with Travis and the Chiefs defeating Jason and the Eagles 38-35. Ed and Donna celebrated with Travis but also had to share the difficult moment with Jason.For Ed, the journey was about much more than watching his sons become famous football players. He had been there when they first started playing sports, helped them through their childhood and continued supporting them when their careers reached the highest level.His story is a reminder that behind many successful athletes are parents who make sacrifices without knowing where their children’s dreams will eventually lead.
Article Summary: Ed Kelce coached Jason and Travis Kelce when they were young. He wanted them to enjoy sports without feeling forced to follow a particular path. Ed and Donna Kelce made sacrifices to give their sons better opportunities. Even when their marriage was going through difficulties, he continued putting his sons first.

Article Title: 'He will regret it after 10 years': Kapil Dev questions Virat Kohli's big decision
Article Text:
virat kohli, kapil dev

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former India captain Kapil Dev has strongly criticised Virat Kohli 's decision to retire from Test cricket, describing it as the biggest mistake of the batting great's career. The legendary all-rounder believes Kohli had plenty left to offer in the longest format, particularly given his exceptional fitness, and feels the 36-year-old could regret walking away from Tests in the years to come.Kohli announced his retirement from Test cricket on May 12, 2025, bringing the curtain down on a career spanning 123 matches. His final appearance in the format came against Australia in Sydney on January 3, 2025. He finished with 9,230 runs at an average of 46.85.Kapil, however, is not convinced that Kohli needed to call time on his Test career. In an interview with Mid-Day, the former India skipper questioned the timing of the decision and suggested that Kohli's physical conditioning should have allowed him to continue playing at the highest level."I think Virat Kohli made the biggest mistake. He retired from Test cricket. He will regret his decision after 10 years. He should not have retired. Kohli has fitness on his side, and his fitness is far better than any other player," Dev said.The 1983 World Cup-winning captain argued that Kohli's fitness gave him an advantage even over much younger cricketers. He also felt that players should respond to difficult phases by fighting their way back into the team rather than choosing retirement."He can challenge even a 25-year-old cricketer on fitness. Getting angry and retiring is not right. They should be like Mohinder Amarnath . He was dropped so many times, but he came back and proved others wrong," Kapil added.By bringing up Mohinder Amarnath's career, Kapil highlighted the importance of perseverance and making a comeback after setbacks. Amarnath experienced several exclusions from the Indian team but repeatedly returned to establish himself, something Kapil believes Kohli could also have attempted instead of walking away from Test cricket.Kohli's Test retirement came after he had already stepped away from T20 Internationals in 2024, following India's T20 World Cup triumph. With his departure from the longest format, the former India captain is now active only in ODI cricket at the international level.Despite moving away from two formats, Kohli continues to remain a key figure in India's 50-over plans. He is scheduled to return to action in the three-match ODI series against Sri Lanka, beginning December 13.The right-hander has enjoyed a productive run in ODIs this year. In 14 matches and 13 innings, he has accumulated 638 runs at an average of 53.17 and a strike rate of over 118. His tally includes two centuries and four half-centuries.
Article Summary: Virat Kohli retired from Test cricket on May 12, 2025. The 36-year-old scored 9,230 runs at an average of 46.85 in 123 matches. Kapil Dev believes Kohli's fitness should have allowed him to continue playing at the highest level.

Article Title: Bam Adebayo injury update: Latest on Miami Heat star’s health after Rockets win
Article Text:
Bam Adebayo. Image via: Issac Baldizon/NBAE via Getty Images

How serious is Bam Adebayo’s hip injury?

Antetokounmpo and Wiggins cover for Adebayo

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Bam Adebayo sat out the second half of Miami’s 128-110 win over the Houston Rockets on Monday night because of right hip tightness. The Heat first listed him as questionable before ruling the 29-year-old center out for the night. Adebayo played about 16 minutes at Kaseya Center and scored four points with two steals. The win was Miami’s fifth in a row, but the early exit took some shine off it. Coach Erik Spoelstra has since given his read on how serious the problem is, and the Heat host Milwaukee on Wednesday.Spoelstra does not expect a long absence. The coach called the move proactive and said he watched Adebayo push through the second quarter, then decided the night was over no matter what anyone said. “I don’t think it’s long term,” Spoelstra said.Miami has not named a diagnosis beyond right hip tightness or given a return date. The plan was to see how Adebayo felt the next day. Adebayo’s availability for Wednesday’s home game against Milwaukee is unclear.Adebayo came into Monday averaging 19.5 points, 8.5 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 2.1 steals. A slow offensive start to the season had given way to better chemistry next to Giannis Antetokounmpo , including 37 points and 14 rebounds against Cleveland on Friday.Against Houston, Adebayo took only three shots in the first half but finished plus-9 as Miami built a 62-46 lead by the break.Spoelstra shifted Antetokounmpo to center and gave Andrew Wiggins the open starting spot to begin the second half. Wiggins finished with 17 points on 6-of-9 shooting, five rebounds and three blocks, and Miami was plus-15 with him on the floor. Antetokounmpo had 20 points, 13 rebounds, six assists and three blocks in roughly 29 minutes, including 14 points in the third quarter, before sitting out the fourth of the blowout.Spoelstra said Antetokounmpo set the tone on offense, finding teammates like Magic Johnson through the opening 14 minutes. The loss goes beyond points, since Adebayo anchors the defense with rim protection, rebounding and the range to guard several positions.The Heat were also without Pelle Larsson, who missed a third straight game with an illness and is expected to be back Wednesday. Across the five-game run, Miami has posted a 126.2 offensive rating, second in the league, and a net rating of 12.5, fourth best. The defense ranks 10th at 113.7, and Spoelstra liked what he saw after holding Houston to 110.Miami is 8-6 after five straight wins and hosts the 1-13 Bucks on Wednesday in Antetokounmpo’s first game against his former franchise.
Article Summary: Bam Adebayo sat out the second half of Miami’s 128-110 win over the Houston Rockets on Monday night because of right hip tightness. The Heat first listed him as questionable before ruling the 29-year-old center out for the night. Coach Erik Spoelstra has since given his read on how serious the problem is.

Article Title: Micah Nori makes intriguing Luka Doncic comparison while revealing what makes LaMelo Ball so special to Minnesota Timberwolves
Article Text:
LaMelo Ball. Image via: Getty Images

Micah Nori compares LaMelo Ball to Luka Doncic

Ball is keeping Minnesota afloat without Edwards

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Micah Nori spent five seasons on Chris Finch’s staff in Minnesota. On Monday, he came back to Minneapolis as the first-year coach of the Portland Trail Blazers, with a 9-3 record and a strong opinion about LaMelo Ball. Nori placed the Timberwolves point guard next to Luka Doncic, though he admitted the comparison might not be perfect. He also described what Ball has done for the mood inside the team facility, and how Finch has taken to it. Portland arrived on a three-game win streak. Both comments came before the game.Nori said LaMelo Ball reminds him of Luka Doncic in one specific way. Opponents know what is coming and still struggle to stop it. Send Ball left and he finds a step-back. Send him right and he gets to the rim or whips a pass to anyone on the floor. Nori called the mix “a problem offensively,” and said it makes life easier for teammates because Ball can go wherever he wants.Preparing for him is no fun, Nori said. He called the All-Star point guard a top-level passer who can also shoot, which means defenders cannot sag off him.Nori also will not overload his players with inside knowledge of Minnesota.He called it unfair to cram everything into one shootaround, since this is one of 82 games. Expect more plays drawn up after timeouts, he said, and Finch will likely do the same because the teams play alike.Ball is in his first season with Minnesota after the Charlotte Hornets traded him in the offseason. Anthony Edwards is sidelined with an injury, and Ball’s play is a major reason the Wolves have stayed afloat in the Western Conference without him.The All-Star guard has played all 13 games, a little over 27 minutes a night, and averages 18.6 points, 3.6 rebounds, 6.2 assists and 1.9 steals. He shoots 43.6 percent from the field, 37.6 percent from three and 78.1 percent at the free-throw line.Nori thinks Ball’s impact goes past the box score. Ball has brought joy to the practice facility, he said, and Finch is having fun with it. Nori could hear it in phone calls with his old boss.Bones Hyland spent a season and a half with Nori in the Timberwolves organization, and the Minnesota guard was blunt about Monday. He called the head coaching job every coach’s dream and pointed to the staff’s back-to-back Western Conference appearances. Then he said the players want to beat their old coach. “Ain’t no bad blood,” Hyland added. Nori’s reply was short: it goes both ways.
Article Summary: Micah Nori spent five seasons on Chris Finch's staff in Minnesota. Ball has brought joy to the practice facility, he said, and Finch is having fun with it. Ball is in his first season with Minnesota after the Charlotte Hornets traded him.

Article Title: Jeffrey Epstein did not commit suicide, was likely killed: Top forensic expert
Article Text:
Freeman claimed that certain marks could only be accounted for by “homicidal strangulation,” (Photo: AP).

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A forensic expert on Monday claimed that convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein was likely killed by someone else and did not die by suicide.Dr Michael Freeman, who reportedly spent a year going through Epstein’s complete autopsy file provided by Epstein’s brother, concluded that Epstein’s injuries “are not explained by a suicidal hanging,” according to the New York Post.He claimed that certain marks could only be accounted for by “homicidal strangulation.”Freeman presented his conclusions at the Middle Temple, a London legal society. The New York Times reported that he said the injuries on Epstein’s body point to a struggle, which contradicts the medical examiner’s findings.Freeman, who gave testimony against former Minneapolis officer Derek Chauvin at his murder trial over George Floyd’s death, pointed to what he described as “fingernail marks” above the ligature line, a bruise at the base of the neck, and a deep, fresh bleeding wound in the left shoulder muscle. In his view, all of these indicate homicide rather than suicide.“I cannot think of a scenario in which he could have caused the spectrum of injuries he has… other than if Epstein himself had wanted to stage his suicide as a homicide,” Freeman told the BBC in an interview.“I believe that the evidence is most consistent with an assault, a ligature strangulation from behind and most probably using that same ligature to suspend the body from the bunk bed.”The New York City medical examiner’s office maintains that it stands by its 2019 conclusion that Epstein took his own life in his Manhattan jail cell.Conspiracy theorists have long maintained that Epstein was murdered inside the Manhattan federal jail to silence him after his arrest on numerous charges that might have put him behind bars for decades.According to Freeman, his “new evidence” stems from details about the position of Epstein’s body when it was discovered and the point where the ligature was anchored. He argued that the injuries normally expected from a hanging in that position do not match those found on Epstein’s body.Freeman did not examine the body himself and has only viewed photographs. He nonetheless argued that he has been able to see the most critical element, the shape and nature of the ligature mark.“Looking at it in person isn’t going to look any different than looking at it in the 30 plus photographs that we have of it,” he told the BBC. “That’s not going to change anything.”Multiple investigations have found no evidence that anyone else was involved.Epstein documents made public in February showed that the New York medical examiner who supervised the autopsy initially hesitated to rule the death a suicide because of the case’s high profile nature.
Article Summary: Dr Michael Freeman spent a year going through Epstein’s complete autopsy file. He said the injuries “are not explained by a suicidal hanging,” according to the New York Post. He claimed that certain marks could only be accounted for by “homicidal strangulation.”

Article Title: Late drama in Bengaluru as Hannan salvages a point against Real Kashmir
Article Text:
In a thrilling Indian Football League match, FC Bengaluru United faced Real Kashmir FC at Bangalore

BENGALURU: There was late drama in the Indian Football League clash between FC Bengaluru United and Real Kashmir FC at the Bangalore Football Stadium here on Saturday. The visitors, leading 2-1, were sniffing victory, but Abdul Hannan had some other plans. The FCBU defender scored the all-important equaliser in the 90th minute.The Snow Leopards went close to scoring the winner in the six added minutes, but FCBU goalkeeper Manjunath Hirekurbar made a double save to salvage a point with a 2-2 draw for the home team.It was RKFC who looked in control during the initial exchanges. They used both the flanks effectively and made their possession count as forward Zahir Khan met Lalawmpuia Sailo’s cross to head into the empty net and take the lead in the 11th minute. However, FCBU regrouped after conceding the goal, and their efforts bore fruit ten minutes later.Colombian Maikol Andres Herrera fancied his chances from 25-odd yards. The long-ranger was out of the reach of Real Kashmir’s diving goalkeeper Susnata Malik to make it all square with a wonder strike into the top bin.It did not take long for the visitors to regain the lead with defender Shanid Valan scoring an outrageous goal.A miskick from midfielder Rohen Singh reached Valan inside the box, and he backheeled the ball above the goalkeeper to stun FCBU players in the 29th minute. Ribhav Sardesai then came close to making it all square, but his curling effort struck the crossbar.At the other end, FCBU defenders also made some last-minute tackles to keep the score 1-2 at the break. RKFC dominated possession for most of the second half, with FCBU being tactically outsmarted. Despite the dominance, they failed to find the net, though they came close with Amzard Khan striking the crossbar. But in the end, it was Hannan who emerged the hero as his late header helped FCBU snatch a draw.
Article Summary: FC Bengaluru United drew 2-2 with Real Kashmir FC at Bangalore Football Stadium. Abdul Hannan scored the all-important equaliser in the 90th minute. The Snow Leopards went close to scoring the winner in the six added minutes, but goalkeeper Manjunath Hirekurbar made a double save.

NEEMRANA: A Canadian woman travelled to Rajasthan hoping to marry a man she had befriended on a dating app. However, the man allegedly refused to marry her after meeting her in person, citing her age.Following a dispute between the two, the woman contacted the Canadian embassy, prompting police to intervene.The incident took place in Neemrana in Rajasthan's Behror district. Police reached the spot around 4am on November 13 after receiving information from the Canadian embassy. They took the woman and the man to the police station for questioning.According to Neemrana SHO Surendra Yadav, Nitin, a resident of Panipat in Haryana and son of Satyanarayan, had started communicating with the Canadian woman through a dating app around a year ago. Their friendship gradually developed into a relationship, and the two agreed to get married.The woman arrived in Delhi on November 11 on a tourist visa. Nitin went to the airport to receive her and brought her to a flat belonging to his maternal uncle and aunt in the BB Builders Society in Neemrana.The woman reportedly stayed with Nitin at the society for two days. However, when discussions about marriage progressed, Nitin allegedly backed out after learning that the woman was around 61 years old.This led to an argument between the two.On November 13, the woman contacted the Canadian embassy and informed officials about the developments. Following the embassy's communication, Neemrana police reached the society and took both of them to the police station.While police are questioning Nitin, the Canadian woman has been shifted to a care centre in Kotputli. Police are also making arrangements for her return to Canada.Nitin is reportedly employed as a teacher at a private school in Panipat. Further investigation into the matter is underway.
Article Summary: Canadian woman travelled to Rajasthan hoping to marry a man she had befriended on a dating app. However, the man allegedly refused to marry her after meeting her in person, citing her age. The woman contacted the Canadian embassy, prompting police to intervene.

Article Title: Delhi showroom murder: CCTV shows victim's final struggle with 'ex-friend' before killing
Article Text:

(With inputs from PTI)





NEW DELHI: A CCTV footage from a clothing showroom in West Delhi's Moti Nagar has captured the final moments of an 18-year-old girl, showing her desperately trying to escape as a man allegedly assaults her before dragging her into a trial room and killing her.The footage reportedly shows the accused, identified as 29-year-old Suraj , repeatedly attacking Shabnam as she screams and attempts to flee. At one point, she sits down and tries to shield herself from the blows, but the man continues assaulting her.He is then seen dragging her by her hair into the trial room, where he allegedly slits her throat.Police arrested Suraj on Sunday and are questioning him to establish the exact motive behind Saturday's murder, including a suspected fallout following a romantic relationship, a police officer said.Shabnam worked at the showroom near Moti Nagar Metro Station. Her body was found inside the trial room by the staff later that evening, police said.According to the preliminary investigation, Shabnam and Suraj were on friendly terms, but their relationship had reportedly turned sour over the past few months. Police are also investigating allegations by the victim's family that the accused had assaulted her earlier.According to accounts shared by people familiar with the incident, Shabnam was seen using her mobile phone at the showroom around 6.45 pm on Saturday.Around 7.30pm, her employer could not locate her and contacted a woman who was Shabnam's former employer, informing her about the assault. The woman then reached the showroom.Some people examined the CCTV footage and noticed that the man had left the premises, but Shabnam had not."Suspecting that she could still be inside, they returned to the showroom around 8.30pm and began searching the premises. During the search, they noticed her scarf lying near the trial room. They also spotted blood seeping out from underneath the door," the officer said.Her body was found around 9pm, following which the police were called.A police team that reached the spot found injury marks on her neck caused by a sharp-edged weapon, along with a blood-stained knife near her body. The body was sent to Deen Dayal Upadhyay Hospital for a post-mortem.Police examined CCTV footage from inside the showroom and nearby areas to piece together the sequence of events, establish the accused's movements and trace his escape route.
Article Summary: CCTV footage shows 18-year-old girl desperately trying to escape as a man allegedly assaults her. He is then seen dragging her by her hair into the trial room, where he allegedly slits her throat. Police arrested Suraj on Sunday and are questioning him to establish the exact motive.

VARANASI: A 2023-batch police sub-inspector, Sandeep Kumar , 28, committed suicide by jumping before a moving train late Saturday evening near Nagpur in Dharampur on the Varanasi-Chhapra rail route in Ballia district.Initial investigation of police exposed that already married Kumar was in extra marital relation with a 22-year-old woman of Sikandarpur, who had been blackmailing him.Ballia SP Iraj Raja on Sunday said that following collection of evidences and lodging of a complaint by Kumar's wife the accused woman Roli Gond was arrested from an orchard near the railway station on the charges of abetment of suicide.Police investigation also cleared that the same woman had also lodged two rape cases against a police constable in past and the latter is still lodged in jail.Earlier, the incident came to light when a train’s loco pilot informed the Chitbaragaon station master through a memo that someone had jumped before his moving train to commit suicide.On being alerted by railway officials Chitbadagaon police and GRP reached the spot, where Kumar's motorbike and mobile phone were found lying near the railway track while his mutilated body was detected on tracks.On getting information Raja, ASP South Sanjay Verma, CO Akshay Kumar and railway police officials also reached there while forensic team was engaged to collect evidence from the railway track area.Kumar, a resident of Sant Kabir Nagar, was married and had a six-month-old child. He had been posted at Chitbaragaon police station for past 11 months.He was transferred to Pakri police station but had not yet been relieved from his old posting because of Chhath festival arrangements. On Saturday evening, he had left police station by informing colleagues that he was going to his duty point.After postmortem examination the mortal remain of Kumar was brought to the police lines, where following guard of honours officials paid tributes and observed silence for two minutes.The officials also consoled Kumar's family, which also remained at police lines.
Article Summary: Sandeep Kumar, 28, committed suicide by jumping before a moving train late Saturday evening near Nagpur in Dharampur on the Varanasi-Chhapra rail route in Ballia district. Initial investigation of police exposed that already married Kumar was in extra marital relation with a 22-year-old woman of Sikandarpur, who had been blackmailing him. Police investigation also cleared that the same woman had also lodged two rape cases against a police constable in past and the latter is still lodged in jail.

Article Text:
Sukhdeep Singh Chhina, who served as the Director of the Punjab Dairy Development Board, has officially stepped down from all roles within the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP)

AAP faces a series of exits in Punjab





CHANDIGARH: The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) has suffered another exit in Punjab , with Sukhdeep Singh Chhina, Director of the Punjab Dairy Development Board, resigning from all party positions and the party's primary membership.Chhina submitted his resignation to AAP Punjab president Aman Arora, formally announcing his decision to sever ties with the party.In his resignation letter addressed to Arora, Chhina wrote: "I, Sukhdeep Singh Chhina, hereby tender my resignation from all positions held in the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and also relinquish my primary membership of the party."The letter does not specify a reason for his decision. Chhina has announced his resignation from party positions and primary membership; the statement provided does not mention whether he is also stepping down as Director of the Punjab Dairy Development Board.Chhina's resignation comes amid a series of departures from the AAP in Punjab. Earlier this month, two party MLAs, Chetan Singh Jouramajra and Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra, resigned from the party's primary membership, a day after AAP announced its first list of 40 candidates for the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections.The two resignations came as the party began preparations for the next Assembly polls. AAP has also faced political criticism and dissent from within its Punjab unit in recent weeks.(With agency inputs)
